newsitem.title: UK: World oil demand up 2.3 pct in '97, close to '96 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: World oil demand up 2.3 pct in '97, close to '96 - IEA.

text.p: World oil demand will rise 2.3 percent or 1.7 million barrels per day (bpd) this year to 73.6 million bpd, a similar rate to that seen last year, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
The IEA, the West's oil watchdog, said that demand had been revised downwards by 200,000 bpd in the first quarter this year due to weak weather-related demand in March.
Demand in OECD countries was expected to rise by 700,000 bpd in the second quarter this year compared to the same period in 1996, the IEA said in its Monthly Oil Market Report for end April.
Demand was projected to be 40.3 million bpd, 1.7 million bpd below the 42.0 million bpd seen in the first quarter this year.
Over the whole of this year OECD demand is projected to rise by 500,000 bpd to 41.6 million bpd, a slower growth rate than in 1996 when demand grew by 700,000 bpd.
The 1997 estimate represented the second successive 100,000 bpd downward revision, primarily due to weather related demand weakness and substitution of fuel oil use in the first quarter this year.
Non-OECD demand was projected to rise by 3.9 percent or 1.2 million bpd to 32 million bpd -- a slightly lower rate of growth than forecast last month, said the IEA.

The growth in global demand was revised downward by 100,000 bpd from last month's report due to a lower estimate of OECD demand in the first quarter, revisions to FSU demand and a small revision upwards to global demand last year.
